stem: Based on these results, which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
stimulus: An astronomy student selected 60 asteroids at random from a catalog of 1,500 main-belt asteroids and looked up the diameter of each one. Based on the sample, the student estimated that the mean diameter of the asteroids in the catalog is 14 kilometers, with an associated margin of error of 3 kilometers.
choices: It is plausible that the mean diameter of all 1,500 asteroids in the catalog is between 11 and 17 kilometers.
It is plausible that every asteroid in the catalog has a diameter between 11 and 17 kilometers.
The mean diameter of all 1,500 asteroids in the catalog is exactly 14 kilometers.
The margin of error means the mean diameter of the 60 sampled asteroids could be anywhere from 11 to 17 kilometers.
explanation: You compute 14 − 3 = 11 and 14 + 3 = 17. The margin of error describes where the mean of the whole catalog plausibly falls, so a mean diameter between 11 and 17 kilometers for all 1,500 asteroids is the supported conclusion.

B.why: You applied the interval to individual asteroids. The margin of error is about the mean diameter, and single asteroids can be much larger or smaller than 11 to 17 kilometers.

C.why: You treated the estimate as exact. A margin of error of 3 kilometers means the true mean is uncertain, so 'exactly 14' claims more than the sample can show.

D.why: You applied the interval to the sample. The sample's mean is known: it is 14 kilometers. The interval estimates the mean of the whole catalog.

stem: Based on these results, which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
stimulus: Ecologists chose 200 trees at random in a forest reserve and checked each one for bark beetle damage. They found damage on 35% of the sampled trees. Based on the sample, they estimated that 35% of the trees in the reserve have beetle damage, with an associated margin of error of 4%.
choices: Exactly 35% of all trees in the reserve have bark beetle damage.
About 4% of the sampled trees were classified incorrectly as damaged or undamaged.
It is plausible that between 31% and 39% of all trees in the reserve have bark beetle damage.
It is plausible that between 31% and 39% of all trees in the state's forests have bark beetle damage.
explanation: You compute 35% − 4% = 31% and 35% + 4% = 39%. Because the trees were sampled only from the reserve, the supported conclusion is that between 31% and 39% of the reserve's trees plausibly have damage.

A.why: You treated the estimate as exact. The 4% margin of error says the true percent is uncertain, so 'exactly 35%' claims more than the data support.

B.why: You read the margin of error as the share of trees that were misclassified. It actually measures the uncertainty from using a sample to estimate the percent for the whole reserve.

D.why: You extended the result beyond the population that was sampled. Only trees in the reserve were sampled, so the conclusion can't cover every forest in the state.

stem: Based on these results, which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
stimulus: A public health department surveyed 150 adults selected at random from a city's residents about their sleep. Based on the survey, the department estimated that the mean nightly sleep of adults in the city is 6.8 hours, with an associated margin of error of 0.4 hours.
choices: Every adult in the city sleeps between 6.4 and 7.2 hours per night.
It is plausible that the mean nightly sleep of all adults in the city is between 6.4 and 7.2 hours.
The mean nightly sleep of all adults in the city is greater than 6.8 hours.
The margin of error means the mean nightly sleep of the 150 sampled adults could be anywhere from 6.4 to 7.2 hours.
explanation: You compute 6.8 − 0.4 = 6.4 and 6.8 + 0.4 = 7.2. The margin of error gives a plausible range for the mean of all adults in the city, so you conclude that this mean is plausibly between 6.4 and 7.2 hours.

A.why: You applied the interval to individual people. Some residents surely sleep 5 hours and others 9. The interval is about the mean only.

C.why: You made a one-sided claim the data can't support. The plausible range includes values below 6.8 as well as above it.

D.why: You applied the interval to the sample. The sample's mean is known to be 6.8 hours. The margin of error describes the city-wide mean.

stem: Based on these results, which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
stimulus: Bird banders captured 50 black-capped chickadees at random from the population wintering in a nature preserve and weighed each bird. Based on the sample, they estimated that the mean mass of the chickadees wintering in the preserve is 11.2 grams, with an associated margin of error of 0.5 grams.
choices: It is not possible that the mean mass of all chickadees wintering in the preserve is above 11.2 grams.
Most chickadees wintering in the preserve have a mass between 10.7 and 11.7 grams.
The margin of error means the mean mass of the 50 captured chickadees could be anywhere from 10.7 to 11.7 grams.
It is plausible that the mean mass of all chickadees wintering in the preserve is between 10.7 and 11.7 grams.
explanation: You compute 11.2 − 0.5 = 10.7 and 11.2 + 0.5 = 11.7. The interval is a plausible range for the mean mass of the whole wintering population in the preserve, so this is the supported conclusion.

A.why: You used a certainty word. Values up to 11.7 grams are inside the plausible range, so a mean above 11.2 grams is certainly possible.

B.why: You applied the interval to individual birds. The margin of error is about the mean mass and says nothing about how most individual birds are spread out.

C.why: You applied the interval to the sample. The 50 captured birds have a known mean of 11.2 grams. The interval estimates the population mean.

stem: Based on these results, which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
stimulus: An agricultural researcher selected 64 tomato plants at random from the 2,000 plants growing in a research greenhouse and weighed each plant's harvest. Based on the sample, the researcher estimated that the mean yield of the plants in the greenhouse is 4.5 kilograms per plant, with an associated margin of error of 0.3 kilograms.
choices: Each plant in the greenhouse yielded between 4.2 and 4.8 kilograms of tomatoes.
The mean yield of all 2,000 plants in the greenhouse is exactly 4.5 kilograms.
It is plausible that the mean yield of all 2,000 plants in the greenhouse is between 4.2 and 4.8 kilograms.
It is plausible that the mean yield of tomato plants in every greenhouse in the region is between 4.2 and 4.8 kilograms.
explanation: You compute 4.5 − 0.3 = 4.2 and 4.5 + 0.3 = 4.8. The sample came from this one greenhouse, so the supported conclusion is that the mean yield of its 2,000 plants is plausibly between 4.2 and 4.8 kilograms.

A.why: You applied the interval to individual plants. Single plants can yield far more or less than the mean. The interval describes only the mean yield.

B.why: You treated the estimate as exact. A margin of error of 0.3 kilograms means the true mean could plausibly be anywhere from 4.2 to 4.8.

D.why: You extended the result beyond the population that was sampled. Only plants in this greenhouse were sampled, so other greenhouses aren't covered.

stem: Based on these results, which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
stimulus: A printmaking studio received a shipment of 5,000 sheets of printmaking paper. The studio manager selected 80 sheets at random from the shipment and measured the thickness of each one. Based on the sample, the manager estimated that the mean thickness of the sheets in the shipment is 0.30 millimeter, with an associated margin of error of 0.02 millimeter.
choices: It is plausible that the mean thickness of all 5,000 sheets in the shipment is between 0.28 and 0.32 millimeter.
Every sheet in the shipment has a thickness between 0.28 and 0.32 millimeter.
The mean thickness of all 5,000 sheets in the shipment is less than 0.30 millimeter.
The margin of error means the mean thickness of the 80 sampled sheets could be anywhere from 0.28 to 0.32 millimeter.
explanation: You compute 0.30 − 0.02 = 0.28 and 0.30 + 0.02 = 0.32. The margin of error gives a plausible range for the mean thickness of the whole shipment, so this is the supported conclusion.

B.why: You applied the interval to individual sheets. Single sheets can fall outside 0.28 to 0.32 millimeter. The interval is about the mean thickness.

C.why: You made a one-sided claim. The plausible range runs from 0.28 to 0.32 millimeter, so the true mean could just as well be above 0.30.

D.why: You applied the interval to the sample. The 80 measured sheets have a known mean of 0.30 millimeter. The interval estimates the mean of the whole shipment.

stem: Based on these results, which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
stimulus: Immunologists selected 300 donors at random from the donors registered with a regional blood bank and tested a sample of each donor's blood for antibodies to a particular virus. Based on the results, they estimated that 18% of the blood bank's registered donors have these antibodies, with an associated margin of error of 3%.
choices: About 3% of the donors who were tested received an incorrect antibody result.
Exactly 18% of all donors registered with the blood bank have antibodies to the virus.
It is plausible that between 15% and 21% of all adults in the country have antibodies to the virus.
It is plausible that between 15% and 21% of all donors registered with the blood bank have antibodies to the virus.
explanation: You compute 18% − 3% = 15% and 18% + 3% = 21%. The donors were sampled from this blood bank's registry, so the supported conclusion is that between 15% and 21% of its registered donors plausibly have the antibodies.

A.why: You read the margin of error as a rate of wrong test results. It measures the uncertainty from estimating the registry-wide percent from a sample.

B.why: You treated the estimate as exact. A 3% margin of error means the true percent could plausibly be anywhere from 15% to 21%.

C.why: You extended the result beyond the population that was sampled. Only this blood bank's registered donors were sampled, not all adults in the country.

stem: Based on these results, which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
stimulus: Urban planners selected 90 of a city's 1,200 signalized intersections at random and recorded how long pedestrians waited for a walk signal at each one. Based on the sample, the planners estimated that the mean pedestrian wait time at the city's signalized intersections is 48 seconds, with an associated margin of error of 6 seconds.
choices: Pedestrians at every signalized intersection in the city wait between 42 and 54 seconds.
It is plausible that the mean wait time across all 1,200 signalized intersections is between 42 and 54 seconds.
The mean wait time across all 1,200 signalized intersections is greater than 48 seconds.
The margin of error means the mean wait time at the 90 sampled intersections could be anywhere from 42 to 54 seconds.
explanation: You compute 48 − 6 = 42 and 48 + 6 = 54. The margin of error gives a plausible range for the mean wait time across all of the city's signalized intersections, so this is the supported conclusion.

A.why: You applied the interval to individual intersections. Some intersections may have much shorter or longer waits. The interval describes only the mean.

C.why: You made a one-sided claim. The plausible range includes values from 42 to 48 seconds too, so the data don't show that the mean is above 48.

D.why: You applied the interval to the sample. The 90 sampled intersections have a known mean of 48 seconds. The interval estimates the city-wide mean.
